memory_update.text: Primary Layer 1B candidates for enterprise AI software/data/workflow node: MSFT, PLTR, NOW, CRM, SNOW.

The strongest direct exposure appears where AI agents must interact with existing enterprise systems: productivity suites, CRM, ITSM, ERP-like workflows, governed data clouds, ontology/data integration, permissioning, and audit trails.

Second-order candidates to evaluate in a separate pass include DDOG for AI/LLM observability, MDB for operational databases and vector search, ORCL and SAP for enterprise systems of record, ADBE for creative/workflow AI, TEAM for collaboration/dev workflows, PANW/CRWD/ZS for AI security, and PATH for RPA/automation.

Need dedicated evidence pass for AI monetization quality: paid attach rate, net revenue retention, usage-based AI revenue, margin drag from inference, AI feature bundling, deployment case studies, and governance/security failure modes.
Add NOW as a high-priority direct candidate for the enterprise AI workflow-orchestration chokepoint; verify AI ACV, attach rate, and incremental monetization.
Add SNOW as a high-priority direct candidate for governed enterprise data substrate; verify Cortex AI consumption, governance adoption, and AI-driven net revenue retention.
Add DDOG as a production AI observability/security candidate; relevance rises if enterprises shift from pilots to monitored production LLM applications and agents.
Add IBM, not CFLT, because IBM completed the Confluent acquisition on March 17, 2026; Confluent exposure is now through IBM rather than a standalone public equity.
Add PATH as a hypothesis-level automation execution layer; require stronger proof that agentic automation is producing incremental ARR rather than narrative relabeling of RPA.
Future passes should separately test cybersecurity/identity/governance vendors such as CRWD, ZS, PANW, OKTA, CYBR, and S as AI-permissioning and agent-access-control chokepoints.

Future passes should separately test vertical software vendors such as VEEV, ADSK, INTU, ADBE, and CRM, where AI deployment may be constrained by domain data, workflow ownership, and regulatory process depth.
SNOW should remain a core candidate for the enterprise AI data layer because governed enterprise data access is a direct bottleneck for AI agents and production GenAI apps.
NOW maps to the workflow automation/action layer of enterprise AI; prioritize evidence around AI attach rate, Pro Plus AI ACV, and agentic workflow deployment quality.
OKTA is a less obvious but potentially important second-order beneficiary because AI agents create non-human identity, cross-app authorization, and permission-governance problems.
DDOG is relevant to production AI because observability, LLM monitoring, agent evaluation, cost monitoring, and incident response are deployment bottlenecks after prototypes move into real workflows.

MDB is a plausible AI application data-layer candidate via integrated operational data, vector search, semantic search, and RAG/agent context infrastructure, but monetization evidence remains less direct.

Important companies not included due to the 5-candidate cap but worth later passes: CRM for Agentforce and Informatica acquisition, PANW for CyberArk/agent identity security exposure, ORCL/SAP/MSFT for enterprise system-of-record control, ESTC for search/RAG/security observability, and PATH for robotic process automation.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the node universe toward US-listed companies with direct exposure to enterprise AI deployment rather than model access alone. The strongest public-market mappings are platforms that already sit inside enterprise workflows, data estates, identity/permission boundaries, governance layers, and operational systems. The top five candidates for this pass are Microsoft, Palantir, Salesforce, ServiceNow, and Snowflake. These are not recommendations; they are research candidates for follow-up evidence checks on AI attach rates, net retention, incremental revenue versus bundled AI cost, customer production deployments, data governance, and margin impact. Expanded the universe around the enterprise AI software/data layer toward companies that can relieve deployment chokepoints: workflow orchestration, governed data clouds, AI observability, real-time data streaming/integration, and agentic automation across legacy systems. The strongest direct exposures in this pass are ServiceNow and Snowflake; Datadog and IBM/Confluent are second-order infrastructure/control-plane suppliers; UiPath is a more contested automation execution layer where evidence must distinguish agentic AI revenue from legacy RPA repositioning. This is research support only, not a trading recommendation. Expanded universe for the AI enterprise deployment layer, emphasizing underappreciated chokepoints around governed enterprise data, AI agent workflow execution, permissions/identity, vector-search-enabled application data, and LLM/agent observability.
